When the colder weather approaches, it's time to pack away your lightweight sleeping bag and bring out your heavier sleeping bag. Even a tent can get a bit too chilly at times, causing your feet and hands to get cold. A sleeping bag liner can help cut down on this discomfort. When used under a full-size sleeping bag, a liner can keep you warm and dry overnight, reducing the effect of condensation and helping protect against mildew and mould. A sleeping bag liner also adds an extra layer between you and your sleeping bag. This offers protection against dirt, dust, animal droppings and insect bites. A sleeping bag liner will help keep your sleeping bag clean, prolonging its life. In general, there are two types of sleeping bag liner - synthetic and down. Sleeping bags may have both an inner and outer liner, as some are thicker than others. Synthetic liners tend to be lighter in weight than down liners because they do not contain down filling. Instead, they are usually a polyester or nylon material. Down liners are ideal when there is limited space to store your sleeping bag, as they are relatively thin and take up less space than other liners. This means you can fit more than one sleeping bag inside a pack without packing another. You may have heard of "fill weight" of a sleeping bag, but what does fill weight mean? Fill weight refers to the weight of the material that makes up the insulation in a sleeping bag. Fill weight matters mainly if you’re trying to carry your sleeping bag with you. In general, a lighter fill weight equals a lower number. The ideal fill weight can differ depending on who you’re asking. For instance, military members might recommend a higher fill weight for cold climates and lower fill weight for warm climates, while backcountry enthusiasts might suggest a lower fill weight for cold weather and higher fill weight for warm weather, as the extra cushioning helps retain body heat and stay warm during rest periods. If you’re planning on using your sleeping bag in extreme cold, you might want to consider an insulated liner or an actual two-shell sleeping bag. There are many pros and cons to sleeping bags with double shells. One of the main benefits is that double-shell bags provide added insulation in very cold weather. The downside of these bags is that they can be quite heavy and bulky, making them harder to transport.
